project.name: AI Interview Prep
project.description: Production-grade AI mock interview preparation platform

modules.name: Project scaffold & configuration
modules.desc: Initialize Next.js 14 App Router with TypeScript strict mode, configure TailwindCSS with shadcn/ui, set up ESLint/Prettier, create the complete folder architecture, configure path aliases, and wire all environment variables.
modules.prompt: Build Module 1 — Project scaffold & configuration: Initialize Next.js 14 App Router with strict TypeScript, configure TailwindCSS + shadcn/ui with components.json, set up the complete src/ folder architecture (app, components, lib, types, hooks, config), configure absolute path aliases in tsconfig.json, create src/config/env.ts with full Zod-validated environment variable schema for Clerk, Gemini, AWS S3, and PostgreSQL, and provide .env.example with all required keys documented.

modules.name: Database schema & Prisma setup
modules.desc: Design and implement the complete PostgreSQL schema using Prisma. Models: User, Resume, JobDescription, Interview, InterviewQuestion, InterviewAnswer, ATSScore, and Feedback. Full relations, indexes, enums, and seed script.
modules.prompt: Build Module 2 — Database schema & Prisma setup: Write the complete prisma/schema.prisma with models for User (clerkId, email, name, imageUrl), Resume (userId, fileName, s3Key, s3Url, parsedText, atsScore), JobDescription (userId, title, company, description, requirements), Interview (userId, resumeId, jobDescriptionId, status enum, totalScore, duration), InterviewQuestion (interviewId, questionText, questionType enum, orderIndex), InterviewAnswer (questionId, answerText, audioS3Key, score, feedback, strengths, improvements), ATSScore (resumeId, jobDescriptionId, overallScore, keywordScore, formatScore, experienceScore, missingKeywords, matchedKeywords, suggestions), and Feedback (interviewId, overallScore, summary, strengths, areasToImprove, communicationScore, technicalScore, confidenceScore). Include all relations, @@index directives, enums, and a prisma/seed.ts. Also write src/lib/db/prisma.ts as a singleton client.

modules.name: Clerk authentication & webhooks
modules.desc: Full Clerk integration: middleware protecting all dashboard routes, sign-in/sign-up pages with Clerk components, webhook endpoint to sync users to PostgreSQL on creation/update/deletion, and a server-side user context utility.
modules.prompt: Build Module 3 — Clerk authentication & webhooks: Write src/middleware.ts using clerkMiddleware() protecting all /dashboard/* routes with a public routes list, both auth page components using Clerk's <SignIn> and <SignUp> with custom appearance config matching the app's design system, the POST /api/webhooks/clerk route.ts that verifies Svix signatures and handles user.created / user.updated / user.deleted events to upsert/delete User records in PostgreSQL via Prisma, and src/lib/auth/get-user.ts — a server utility that calls currentUser() from Clerk and returns the matching Prisma User record, throwing a redirect to sign-in if unauthenticated.

modules.name: App shell & layout system
modules.desc: Root layout with font configuration, dashboard layout with sidebar navigation (collapsible), topbar with user avatar/dropdown, mobile responsive drawer, loading skeletons, error boundaries, and the global toast/notification provider.
modules.prompt: Build Module 4 — App shell & layout system: Create src/app/layout.tsx as the root layout with ClerkProvider, custom Google Fonts (use a premium pairing like DM Sans + DM Serif Display), Toaster provider, and metadata. Create src/app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx with a fixed sidebar and scrollable main content area. Build src/components/layout/sidebar.tsx with navigation items (Dashboard, Resume, Interviews, Analytics), active state detection via usePathname, collapse toggle, and UserButton from Clerk at the bottom. Build src/components/layout/topbar.tsx with breadcrumbs and a notification bell. Build src/components/layout/mobile-nav.tsx as a Sheet-based drawer. Add reusable skeleton components and an error boundary wrapper. All components must be fully responsive (mobile-first) using Tailwind.

modules.name: S3 file upload pipeline
modules.desc: Presigned URL generation endpoint, client-side multipart upload with react-dropzone, upload progress tracking, file type/size validation (Zod), S3 bucket configuration with proper CORS, and a server action to persist S3 metadata to the Resume model.
modules.prompt: Build Module 5 — S3 file upload pipeline: Write src/lib/storage/s3.ts initializing the AWS S3Client with credentials from env config and exporting helper functions: generatePresignedUploadUrl(key, contentType, expiresIn) using PutObjectCommand + getSignedUrl, generatePresignedDownloadUrl(key), and deleteObject(key). Write the POST /api/upload/route.ts that validates the request body with Zod (fileName, fileType, fileSize with limits: PDF/DOCX ≤10MB), generates a presigned URL, and returns it with the S3 key. Write src/components/resume/upload-dropzone.tsx as a full client component using react-dropzone: drag-and-drop zone, file preview with name/size, upload progress bar (XMLHttpRequest to presigned URL for real progress), error states, and success callback that triggers the server action to save metadata. Write the server action in src/lib/actions/resume.ts that creates the Resume record in Prisma after upload completes.

modules.name: PDF parsing & text extraction
modules.desc: Server-side PDF and DOCX text extraction using pdf-parse. Extracts raw text from S3 files, cleans and normalizes the content, stores parsed text back to the Resume record, and exposes a re-parse action.
modules.prompt: Build Module 6 — PDF parsing & text extraction: Write src/lib/ai/resume-parser.ts that downloads a file from S3 by key using GetObjectCommand, converts the stream to a Buffer, uses pdf-parse to extract raw text from PDFs, implements a cleanResumeText(raw: string) function that normalizes whitespace, removes garbled characters, and preserves section structure. Write src/lib/actions/parse-resume.ts as a Next.js server action that takes a resumeId, fetches the Resume from Prisma, downloads and parses the file, updates the Resume.parsedText field, and returns the cleaned text. Handle errors gracefully with typed error returns using a Result<T, E> pattern.

modules.name: ATS scoring engine
modules.desc: Gemini-powered ATS analysis: keyword extraction from job description, semantic matching against resume text, scoring across 5 dimensions (keywords, format, experience, skills, education), missing keyword detection, and full structured output with improvement suggestions.
modules.prompt: Build Module 7 — ATS scoring engine: Write src/lib/ai/gemini.ts initializing the Google Generative AI client (gemini-1.5-pro) with a reusable generateStructuredOutput<T>(prompt, schema) helper that enforces JSON responses and parses them safely. Write src/lib/ai/ats-scorer.ts with a scoreResumeAgainstJob(resumeText, jobDescription) function that calls Gemini with a detailed system prompt instructing it to act as an expert ATS system, return a strictly typed JSON with: overallScore (0-100), keywordScore, formatScore, experienceScore, skillsScore, educationScore (each 0-100), matchedKeywords: string[], missingKeywords: string[], suggestions: {category, priority, text}[], and summary: string. Write src/lib/actions/ats-score.ts as a server action that orchestrates fetching the Resume + JobDescription, calling the scorer, and upserting an ATSScore record. Write the POST /api/ats-score/route.ts as a streaming endpoint.

modules.name: Resume management dashboard page
modules.desc: Full resume management page: upload flow, resume list with cards (filename, upload date, ATS score badge), resume detail view with parsed text preview, ATS score breakdown with radial charts, keyword match visualization, and improvement suggestions panel.
modules.prompt: Build Module 8 — Resume management dashboard page: Write src/app/(dashboard)/resume/page.tsx as a server component that fetches all resumes for the current user with their ATSScores. Render a two-column layout: left panel is the upload dropzone (Module 5 component) + resume list using ResumeCard components; right panel is a detail view. Build src/components/resume/resume-card.tsx showing file name, company/role if linked to a job, upload date, and an ATS score badge (color-coded: red <50, amber 50-75, green >75). Build src/components/resume/ats-score-display.tsx showing the overall score with a large circular progress ring (SVG-based, no library), five sub-score bars with labels, and an expandable suggestions list. Build src/components/resume/keyword-match.tsx showing matched keywords as green chips and missing keywords as red chips. All components use shadcn/ui primitives, Tailwind, and proper loading/error states with Suspense.

modules.name: Interview configuration & question generation
modules.desc: Interview setup form (role, difficulty, type, duration, resume + JD selection), Gemini-powered question generation tailored to resume and JD context, question bank persistence, and interview session initialization.
modules.prompt: Build Module 9 — Interview configuration & question generation: Write src/app/(dashboard)/interview/new/page.tsx as a server component that fetches the user's resumes and job descriptions for selection. Build src/components/interview/interview-setup-form.tsx as a multi-step form (react-hook-form + Zod) with: Step 1 — select resume + paste/select job description, Step 2 — configure interview type (Technical/Behavioral/Mixed), difficulty (Junior/Mid/Senior), number of questions (5/10/15), and focus areas (checkboxes). On submit, call the server action. Write src/lib/ai/question-generator.ts with generateInterviewQuestions(config: InterviewConfig) that sends a detailed Gemini prompt with the resume text and job description, instructing it to generate contextually relevant questions with questionType (technical/behavioral/situational), difficulty, expectedTopics, and followUpHints. Write src/lib/actions/interview.ts with createInterview() server action that persists the Interview + all InterviewQuestion records.

modules.name: Live interview session UI
modules.desc: Real-time interview conductor: question display with timer, text answer input with character count, question progress indicator, pause/resume controls, session state machine (not-started → in-progress → completed), and keyboard shortcuts.
modules.prompt: Build Module 10 — Live interview session UI: Write src/app/(dashboard)/interview/[id]/page.tsx as a server component that fetches the Interview with all InterviewQuestions and passes it as a prop. Build src/components/interview/interview-conductor.tsx as the main client component managing session state with useReducer: states are 'ready', 'answering', 'submitting', 'completed'. Show one question at a time. Write src/hooks/use-interview-session.ts managing: currentQuestionIndex, answers array, per-question elapsed time (setInterval), total elapsed time, and a submitAnswer(questionId, answerText) function that calls a server action and advances to the next question. Build src/components/interview/question-display.tsx showing the question text, type badge, a countdown timer (configurable per question), and hint reveal toggle. Build src/components/interview/answer-input.tsx as a rich textarea with character count, Ctrl+Enter to submit, and a submit button. Build src/components/interview/progress-tracker.tsx as a step indicator showing answered/current/upcoming questions.

modules.name: AI answer evaluation engine
modules.desc: Per-answer Gemini evaluation: scores answer quality, relevance, depth, communication across 5 rubrics, extracts strengths and improvement points, generates follow-up suggestions, and persists structured feedback to InterviewAnswer.
modules.prompt: Build Module 11 — AI answer evaluation engine: Write src/lib/ai/answer-evaluator.ts with evaluateAnswer(question, answer, resumeContext, jobContext) that calls Gemini with a structured rubric prompt. The prompt instructs Gemini to evaluate the answer on: relevance (0-10), depth (0-10), clarity (0-10), technical accuracy (0-10 if applicable), and structure (STAR method compliance for behavioral). Return typed JSON: { score: number, rubricScores: {...}, strengths: string[], improvements: string[], idealAnswerOutline: string[], followUpQuestions: string[], verdict: 'excellent'|'good'|'needs-improvement'|'poor' }. Write src/lib/actions/evaluate-answer.ts as a server action that takes questionId + answerText, fetches context (question, interview, resume, jobDescription), calls the evaluator, and upserts the InterviewAnswer record with all evaluation fields. Write the streaming POST /api/interview/evaluate/route.ts that evaluates and streams back the response using ReadableStream for real-time UI updates.

modules.name: Interview completion & summary
modules.desc: Post-interview summary screen: overall score calculation, per-question score breakdown table, strongest/weakest answer highlights, time statistics, and CTA to view full feedback report or retake.
modules.prompt: Build Module 12 — Interview completion & summary: Write src/lib/actions/complete-interview.ts as a server action that marks the Interview as completed, calculates the overallScore as a weighted average of all InterviewAnswer scores, updates Interview.totalScore and Interview.duration, and triggers a background feedback generation job (call the feedback generator server action). Build src/components/interview/interview-summary.tsx as the completion screen shown after the last question: large animated score reveal (count-up animation using requestAnimationFrame), a performance verdict badge, 3 key stats (avg score, total time, questions answered). Build src/components/interview/score-breakdown-table.tsx showing each question with its score bar, verdict badge, and a preview of the top strength — clicking a row opens an accordion with the full evaluation. Include 'View Full Report' and 'Start New Interview' CTAs.

modules.name: Comprehensive AI feedback report
modules.desc: Gemini-generated holistic interview feedback: executive summary, communication score, technical depth score, confidence indicators, top 3 strengths, top 3 growth areas, personalized study plan with resources, and a shareable PDF report.
modules.prompt: Build Module 13 — Comprehensive AI feedback report: Write src/lib/ai/feedback-generator.ts with generateInterviewFeedback(interviewId) that collects all questions + answers + individual scores, then prompts Gemini to synthesize a holistic report as typed JSON: { overallScore, executiveSummary, communicationScore, technicalScore, confidenceScore, problemSolvingScore, strengths: {title, description, example}[], areasToImprove: {title, description, actionPlan}[], studyPlan: {topic, resources: {title,url}[], priority}[], interviewReadiness: 'ready'|'almost-ready'|'needs-preparation' }. Write the server action. Build src/app/(dashboard)/feedback/[id]/page.tsx as a server component. Build src/components/feedback/feedback-report.tsx as a comprehensive report layout with tabbed sections (Overview, Per-Question, Study Plan). Build src/components/feedback/score-radar-chart.tsx using Recharts RadarChart with 5 axes. Build src/components/feedback/study-plan.tsx as an actionable checklist with priority badges and resource links.

modules.name: Analytics dashboard
modules.desc: User performance analytics: score trends over time (line chart), interview frequency heatmap, per-skill radar chart evolution, ATS score history, top weak areas aggregated across all interviews, and performance percentile.
modules.prompt: Build Module 14 — Analytics dashboard: Write src/lib/actions/analytics.ts with getUserAnalytics(userId) that queries Prisma for: all completed interviews with scores, all ATS scores over time, aggregated skill scores (avg communication, technical, confidence per week), most common weak areas across all feedback. Build src/app/(dashboard)/analytics/page.tsx as a server component using Suspense for each section. Build src/components/analytics/stats-overview.tsx showing 4 metric cards: total interviews, avg score, best score, improvement trend (% change last 30 days). Build src/components/analytics/score-trend-chart.tsx as a Recharts LineChart with interview date on X-axis, overall score on Y-axis, a reference line at 70 (target), and tooltips showing interview details. Build src/components/analytics/skill-radar.tsx as a Recharts RadarChart comparing current vs previous period averages across 5 skills. All charts use the app's color palette via CSS variables and have proper empty states.

modules.name: Job description management
modules.desc: Job description CRUD: paste or type JD, auto-extract role/company/requirements with Gemini, save to library, link to resumes for ATS scoring, and a JD detail view showing matched resume scores.
modules.prompt: Build Module 15 — Job description management: Write src/lib/ai/jd-extractor.ts with extractJobDescriptionMetadata(rawText) that calls Gemini to parse and return: { title, company, location, salaryRange, requiredSkills: string[], preferredSkills: string[], experienceLevel, responsibilities: string[], requirements: string[] } as typed JSON. Write src/lib/actions/job-description.ts with createJobDescription, updateJobDescription, deleteJobDescription server actions (all auth-protected with Zod validation). Build the page as a two-panel layout: left is a list of saved JDs as cards showing title, company, number of linked resumes; right panel is the create/edit form. Build src/components/resume/job-description-form.tsx as a react-hook-form form with a large textarea for pasting JD text and an 'Auto-extract details' button that calls the AI extractor and populates the fields. On save, auto-run ATS scoring against all user resumes.

modules.name: Main dashboard overview page
modules.desc: The /dashboard landing page: welcome banner, quick-action cards (upload resume, start interview, view analytics), recent interviews list, latest ATS scores, performance summary widget, and empty states for new users.
modules.prompt: Build Module 16 — Main dashboard overview page: Write src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx as a server component that in parallel fetches (Promise.all): user profile, recent 5 interviews with scores, latest 3 ATS scores, and performance analytics summary. Build a responsive grid layout. Build src/components/shared/quick-actions.tsx as 3 prominent action cards with icons: 'Upload Resume' (links to /resume), 'Start Mock Interview' (links to /interview/new), 'View Analytics' (links to /analytics) — each with a description and a visual indicator (green if setup complete, amber if incomplete). Build src/components/shared/recent-interviews.tsx as a table/list of recent interviews with role, date, score badge, status, and a 'View Report' link. Build src/components/shared/performance-summary.tsx as a mini stat panel. Build src/components/shared/empty-state.tsx as a reusable empty state component with illustration, heading, body text, and optional CTA button — used across all pages when no data exists.

modules.name: SEO, metadata & landing page
modules.desc: Public-facing landing page with hero, features, pricing section, and testimonials. Full Next.js metadata API integration, OpenGraph tags, sitemap.xml, robots.txt, and structured data for SEO.
modules.prompt: Build Module 17 — SEO, metadata & landing page: Write src/app/sitemap.ts and src/app/robots.ts. Update src/app/layout.tsx with full Next.js Metadata API: title template, description, OpenGraph (og:image, og:type), Twitter card, canonical URL, and structured data (JSON-LD for SoftwareApplication). Build src/app/page.tsx as a polished public landing page with: a hero section (headline, subheadline, two CTAs: 'Start Free' → /sign-up, 'See Demo' → scroll), a features grid (6 feature cards with icons), a how-it-works 3-step section, an ATS score demo widget, a pricing section (Free / Pro / Team tiers with feature comparison), and a footer. All sections use framer-motion scroll-triggered animations (viewport: { once: true }). The design should be premium and distinct — avoid generic SaaS purple gradients.

modules.name: Performance optimization & error handling
modules.desc: Route-level code splitting, React Suspense boundaries on every async page, global error.tsx and not-found.tsx, rate limiting on AI endpoints, API response caching with Next.js cache tags, Prisma query optimization with select/include, and a health check endpoint.
modules.prompt: Build Module 18 — Performance optimization & error handling: Write src/app/error.tsx and src/app/(dashboard)/error.tsx as proper error boundaries with reset functionality. Write src/app/not-found.tsx with a helpful 404 page linking back to dashboard. Write src/lib/rate-limit.ts implementing a sliding window rate limiter using a Map with TTL cleanup — applyRateLimit(identifier, limit, windowMs) — apply it to all AI API routes. Write src/lib/cache.ts with typed wrappers around Next.js unstable_cache: cacheUserAnalytics(userId), cacheATSScore(resumeId, jdId) with proper revalidation tags. Write src/lib/db/queries/optimized.ts consolidating all heavy Prisma queries with proper select fields (never fetch parsedText in list views), cursor-based pagination helper, and a getInterviewWithFullDetails(id) query using nested includes. Write src/app/api/health/route.ts checking DB connectivity and returning status 200/503. Add Suspense boundaries with custom skeleton fallbacks to all dashboard pages.
